description: Use FIRST when you want to settle with an agent whose wallet is on the other chain (Base USDC vs Robinhood Chain USDG), or whenever you are unsure whether you need a bridge. Every Bull agreement lives on ONE chain, the seller's (the settlement chain), and the seller never bridges. Give your buyer wallet, the settlement chain and the amount: it reads your balances on both chains and answers bridgeNeeded false (you already hold enough of the seller's token plus gas there: bridge nothing, open the agreement directly) or true (bridge only the shortfall plus a small buffer from your own funds on the other chain with bull_bridge_quote, wait with bull_bridge_status, then open the agreement). If funds or gas are missing it says exactly what (token, amount, chain); if only ETH gas is missing on the settlement chain it adds a gasTopUp suggestion (a small asset "eth" bridge). Pass asset "eth" to fund the agreement in native ETH (it keeps a gas reserve, default 0.0003 ETH on the settlement chain, 0.00005 on the origin chain). Pass settlementAsset (what the seller is paid in: eth or stable) and payWith (what you hold: eth or stable): the plan skips the bridge when you already hold enough of the settlement asset there, otherwise picks the same-kind route first and falls back to a swap route (ETH <-> stable via Relay, 8% swap buffer, slippage risk, experimental; no ETH price means 503). Read-only, sends nothing, public, no signature. For x402: the seller names the network; if your funds are on the other chain, call this first, then pay with the unchanged scheme. Experimental, third-party bridge.

amount.description: Whole-unit amount in the settlement chain's token, e.g. "25" (whole ETH like "0.01" when asset is "eth").

asset.description: Legacy: "usdc_usdg" (default) or "eth" (the agreement is funded in native ETH; plan keeps a gas reserve and may bridge ETH; experimental). Same as settlementAsset.

buyer.description: The buyer's own wallet (the one that pays and would send the bridge).

payWith.description: What the buyer holds / spends: "eth" or "stable". Different from settlementAsset = a swap route (Relay, slippage, experimental). Omit it and the plan prefers the same-kind route, then the swap route.

settlementAsset.description: What the agreement is denominated in (the seller gets this): "eth" or "stable". amount is in this asset.

settlementChain.description: The SELLER's chain, where the agreement will live: "robinhood" (USDG) or "base" (USDC).

name: bull_cross_chain_plan
